item.title: Reentrancy attacks explained: every variant, and why guards aren't enough
item.dc:creator: SENTRYX Research
item.description: Single-function, cross-function, cross-contract and read-only reentrancy — with the code that breaks, the code that fixes it, and the cases where a nonReentrant modifier gives you false confidence.

item.title: Oracle manipulation: how a flash loan turns a price feed into an exploit
item.dc:creator: SENTRYX Research
item.description: Why spot prices from AMM reserves are not prices, what TWAP actually protects against, and the Chainlink integration checks that most teams skip.

item.title: Access control failures: the simplest bug class, and the most expensive
item.dc:creator: SENTRYX Research
item.description: Missing modifiers, callable initializers, tx.origin authentication and admin keys that can do more than anyone realised. Plus how to design roles that survive an upgrade.

item.title: Share price inflation and rounding: how vaults leak value one wei at a time
item.dc:creator: SENTRYX Research
item.description: The first-depositor attack, donation attacks, rounding direction, and why 'it's only a wei' stops being true when an attacker can repeat it a million times.

item.title: MEV and front-running: when correct code still loses users money
item.dc:creator: SENTRYX Research
item.description: Sandwich attacks, liquidation races, weak commit-reveal and the protocol design decisions that decide how much value leaks to searchers before a user's transaction lands.

item.title: Upgradeable contracts: storage collisions, uninitialised proxies and admin risk
item.dc:creator: SENTRYX Research
item.description: Transparent, UUPS and diamond patterns compared by failure mode — storage layout rules, initializer safety, and why your upgrade path is part of your attack surface.
